title: The knowledge ecosystem
html:
English | Português (Brasil)

The knowledge ecosystem

Tutorial 05 told what remains when the project ends. This page opens the ecosystem: where the knowledge lives, who writes into it, and how an artifact finds its place.

The three shelves of the state pack

MinhaOrganizacao' knowledge lives in a state pack — a Git repository cloned at packs/<id>/ in the engine config, inherited by the team via golmet pack update. Inside it, three shelves with defined owners and formats: domains/ (the foundation — domain knowledge researched from primary sources, with URL and access date, written by gm-domain-research BEFORE any component consumes the domain), accumulation/ (the learning — patterns extracted by gm-pattern-extractor, metrics by gm-metrics-collector, nuances by gm-nuance-collector) and rules/ (the norms with triggers, written by gm-rule-keeper — see profile.md).

The separation isn't bureaucracy — each shelf has a different life cycle: the foundation changes slowly (the domain doesn't change every week), the learning grows with every project, the norms consolidate when the team decides.

The router: where it goes

Mid-work, an artifact appears with no obvious destination — the discovery "we deploy this way" could be a nuance, a pattern or a norm. The question is not the operator's: the router (the gm-knowledge-route skill, guided by the AGENTS.md T1–T5 table) classifies the fit and delegates to the canonical writer — each shelf has ONE writer, never two. The central rule: route, never replicate — each shelf has its own index, and copying content between them is the road to knowledge rotting into two different versions.

The escape valve covers what fits nothing: the artifact is born in the work zone (.golmet/) — never loose — and is promoted when it gains a function, with the canonical writer responsible for the promotion.

Why a pack and not a loose folder

A state pack is a Git repository of its own: pack publish pushes to the remote, pack update pulls for the team — with auto-commit of the local accumulation and rebase, and the kit never discards what the team accumulated. That is the difference between knowledge living in a file nobody versions and knowledge living in a versioned organizational asset.
